messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
I'm Pranayan Metiya

pranayan metiya... that's a name with some serious character. sounds like someone who gets things done.

where you working these days?
Will you share open roles by yourself, or do I need to text first and only then you'll respond

yo pranayan, once you're in the system, roles drop directly in chat. no need to beg for them.

but first i need to actually know who you are. can't match you to roles if i don't know your background.

so... where you working? or if you're a student, which college?
I'm working at Loop AI, which is a Us based series a startup on a very high growth trajectory

loop ai... us-based series a on high growth trajectory. love the optimism. building something that actually matters or just another ai wrapper?

found you on linkedin - pranayan metiya, software engineer at loop ai. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/pranayan-metiya-75b12a1a3
Well you can ask the 300+ restaurant chains Who pay us and the 12k locations we serve

300+ restaurant chains, 12k locations... okay that's actually legit scale. not just another ai wrapper then.

found you on linkedin - pranayan metiya, software engineer at loop ai. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/pranayan-metiya-75b12a1a3
Yes

software engineer at loop ai... building the tech that powers restaurant operations at serious scale. 300+ chains don't trust just anyone with their operations. that's solid work.

what got you into the restaurant tech space? seems like a pretty specific industry to land in.

hey pranayan, was just thinking about your work at loop ai - 300+ restaurant chains is no joke. that's real impact.

so what's the dream next step for you? looking for more scale, different tech stack, or just chasing that next-level challenge?
I want to work more on AI stuff - agents, mcp servers etc

2 years as a full time engineer

2 years... perfect timing actually. you're past the junior phase but not locked into any one stack yet. prime time to pivot into proper ai work.

what kind of role you looking for next? more backend/infra building the agent systems, or frontend making them actually usable, or something else?
Did you die

lmaooo nah still here, just processing that you've got 2 years under your belt and want to move into ai agents

so back to business - what kind of role you targeting next? backend building the agent infrastructure, frontend making ai actually usable for humans, or something completely different?
Mostly backend stuff. And not exclusively AI, I'm equally interested in AI, infra and product engineering

backend with that mix... smart. ai without infra is just demos, and product eng keeps you grounded in what users actually need.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Prefer remote
2 years experience + backend focus + ai/infra/product engineering + remote preferred... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yep
you're in, legend!
now i've got your radar locked on the good stuff. backend roles at companies that actually understand ai + infra. remote-friendly places that won't make you pretend to love the office.

Yep
  Do you have salary info about the roles?

salary info depends on the role - some companies share it upfront, others hide it until later.

what's your current range? helps me filter out the lowball offers.

30 lakhs base
  I won't accept anything offering less than 40 lpa inr base

40 LPA base minimum, currently at 30. that's a solid jump but doable with the right ai/infra roles.

noted. i'll filter out anything that doesn't hit that mark.

found an AI automation engineer role building agents and LLM workflows

direct CTO reporting and you'd be automating HR/finance ops for a fintech client

salary not listed though, need to check if it hits your 40 LPA base

Pretty good

agno framework with clickhouse... that's legit. you're working with modern agent tooling.
